what_happened: The person running Athena set origin/HEAD to main by hand in Athena's working copy. A newly landed baseline-reuse step finds main's GitHub check result by looking up origin/HEAD. This clone never had that ref, so the lookup found nothing. The first job after the fix therefore re-ran the 20-minute baseline anyway. No job was rejected or failed. No acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. This was an environment gap found when the speed-up did not take effect.
cause: The baseline-reuse code assumed a clone property (origin/HEAD) that a plain clone or fetch setup does not guarantee. Nothing in setup or at startup creates the ref or checks that it exists. The lookup treats a missing ref as "no baseline to reuse" and quietly runs the full baseline, so the failure looks like normal behavior. Tests used fixtures that had the ref, and no end-to-end check showed that reuse actually happened on the real clone. The gap was only noticed from the unchanged 20-minute run time.
prevention: Make the baseline-reuse step resolve the default branch without depending on origin/HEAD. It would try origin/HEAD, then fall back to the configured main branch name, and set origin/HEAD itself if it is missing. Setup and `athena doctor` would also check that the ref exists. When reuse is skipped because a lookup failed, the step would record a visible reason in the job record, such as "no baseline: origin/HEAD missing", instead of silently re-running. Add a test that runs the lookup in a clone with no origin/HEAD and asserts that reuse still happens, or that the reason is recorded.
proposed_request: Make the baseline-reuse step work in a clone that has no origin/HEAD. Outcome: when Athena looks up main's GitHub check result to reuse as the baseline, it finds the default branch even if origin/HEAD is not set. It tries origin/HEAD first, then the configured default branch name, and sets origin/HEAD itself when it is missing. If it still cannot find a result to reuse, the job record states the reason, for example "no baseline reused: default branch not resolved", so the person running Athena can see why the 20-minute baseline ran. Also add a check to `athena doctor` or setup that reports when origin/HEAD is missing. Acceptance: (1) a test that runs the baseline lookup in a clone with no origin/HEAD and shows the baseline is reused from main's result; (2) a test that shows a recorded reason when no result can be found; (3) the doctor or setup check reports a missing origin/HEAD and passes once it is set. Do not change how baselines are judged. Keep the change to the baseline-reuse code, the doctor or setup check, and their tests.
